subject.title: fix(memory-core): honor private-network settings for OpenAI-compatible embeddings

question: Should configured OpenAI-compatible memory embeddings use exact-origin trust when `request.allowPrivateNetwork` is omitted, fail closed when it is false, and allow broader private-network access when it is true?
rationale: The implementation and proof establish the behavior, but this three-state SSRF and upgrade contract requires explicit maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve the three-state contract
options.body: Adopt provider-inherited exact-origin trust, explicit denial, and explicit broad opt-in as the canonical memory embedding policy.

options.title: Preserve hostname compatibility
options.body: Keep omitted policy hostname-scoped while continuing to honor explicit false and true.

options.title: Require explicit opt-in
options.body: Block all private embedding endpoints unless `allowPrivateNetwork` is explicitly true.

recommendation.title: Approve the three-state contract
recommendation.body: Adopt provider-inherited exact-origin trust, explicit denial, and explicit broad opt-in as the canonical memory embedding policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Kaspre introduced the merged origin-scoped provider SSRF contract that most directly defines this policy choice.
